issue.title: v0.6.7 hardware P0: knob/encoder and button latency while audio and visual rendering remain smooth
issue.body:
## New actual FM-1 owner regression, 2026-11-07
> "I am also noticing lagg with the controls.. knobs selecting and button presses, etc... the audio and visuals seem fine though besides that..."

The concern is **input-to-action latency and missed/multiple encoder/button input during playback**, not audio skipping or apparent video stutter. Owner reports audio/visual smoothness; preserve it. Treat as release-blocking usability regression until measured and repaired.

### Evidence and suspects to investigate (not yet proven cause)
- `device/app.c::app_frame()` starts with `app_input_only()`, then services preference-save polling, arrangement, AIR, telemetry, `prepare_geometry()`, and finally synchronous `draw(animate)`. A long graphics/worker/transfer cycle can delay the **next** input poll even if animation looks steady.
- `app_input_only()` polls `plat_buttons`, `plat_keys` and seven `plat_enc` per pass; inspect input scan accumulation/overflows, debounce, event edge capture, queued commands, processing after visual jobs and long flash-store operations. `prepare_geometry` waits for CPU2 work and falls back to CPU1 when needed; separate render scheduling from prompt input processing.
- Page first-input wake in fullscreen currently discards encoder deltas (`if(fullscreen){fullscreen=0; ... for 7 enc set 0;}`); distinguish this intentional wake from real steady-page latency. Confirm behavior owner expects on wake.
- Log per input type (SELECT, Algo, Preset, K1–4, PLAY, EDIT, HOME, SEL) in PLAY/SOUND/MIX/DRUMS/SETUP, fullscreen and nonfullscreen, Chladni/Cymatics/Original, music active and STOP: **physical event -> queue acknowledgement -> audio-state change -> LCD label updated**. Capture p50/p95/p99 max, missed events, queue fullness, redraw and DMA frame timing, inter-core wait, persistence-save stalls. Determine acceptable responsiveness targets from prior v0.6.6 owner-perceived fast baseline, not invented fixed hardware promises.
- Repair by bounded scheduling / priority to inputs, nonblocking optional visual work, preserving audio ISR and scan timing. Avoid heavy new service loops, flashing during ISR or regressions to brightness/pending-key behavior. Verify no accidental double actions and all controls display live values.

### Acceptance
Reproduce with scripted rapid/slow knob turns and button taps at low/high CPU, a long-press, mode switch, 20 FPS fullscreen, delayed DMA and forced single-core; compare actual hardware feel with v0.6.6. Owner acceptance unverified until physical retest. Do not mark solved with audio-frame or FPS-only benchmarks. Keep published releases intact; no duplicate builder; KIRA-9 untouched; MIDI deferrals unchanged.

Related #35 SOUND/SELECT, #32 requirement matrix, #37/#38 visual work and #39 safe settings persistence.

issue.body:
## Real FM-1 owner listening report — v0.6.7, Nov 7 2026
> "There seems to be dead spots now... areas where only the soundscapes are active..."

The user wants coherent *ambient electronic music*, not endless continuous loudness; legitimate purposeful sparse breaks are fine. **But accidental extended disappearance of all pitched/rhythmic instrumentation while Nature/FX continues is not.** A passage must sound like a deliberate musically resolved interlude, not a stalled generator.

### Code-level likely contributor; confirm with rendered stems
- `device/dsp/engine.c::song_section` currently uses a short repeated section form and `plan_roles` sets `role_target[SR_BASS]=(section==3)?0:1`; `role_target[SR_DRUMS]=(section==1||section==2||section==4)?1:0`. At section 3, **both bass and drums are explicitly off**; other roles become less likely by division of eligibility probabilities (except Drone/Choir). In low-energy/mode combinations, this can plausibly yield long Nature-only stretches. Do not claim this is the sole proven cause until post-gain audio is inspected.
- Need explicit intent/style-aware arrangement guardrails: musical through-line via melodic, harmonic, bass or rhythm anchor, except when the selected intention/style truly requests a **short planned beatless passage**. If nature-only interlude intended, expose section name/timing and ensure musically motivated entry/exit and return; never random indefinite gap. No mandatory all eight roles playing.
- Inspect role targets AND accepted notes, gain envelopes, patch ADSR, solo/mute, FX/nature isolation, voice steals, stamina, and actual post-mix audible stems. Avoid faking meter values or just boosting Nature.
- Develop an original phrasing policy: deliberate intro/groove/bloom/hush/bridge/return dynamics, melodic/harmonic continuity, groove anchored where intended, smooth re-entry, energy trajectory and small fills. Compare all 21 intentions, 3 modes, 16/32/64, Freeze/Evolve, bank recall, New Song/Reroll, seeds and long-session timeline. Preserve existing natural pauses and user mute/lock behavior.
- Test measured **Nature-only duration, number of consecutive bars with no meaningful pitched or drum output, track-event count vs actual post-gain RMS**, density of unintended dead zones and transitions. Analyze same-seed v0.6.6 vs v0.6.7 vs corrected. Run owner listening kit for calm versus rhythmic presets to judge if intentional rests have musical purpose; physical aesthetic acceptance pending.
- Protect 0.6.7 audio and video smoothness, all sound-healing intention tuning, exact Hz/reference frequencies and binaural separation. Original implementation only; don't copy copyrighted third-party source/music.

issue.body:
## Owner artistic direction — first real FM-1 v0.6.7 review, 2026-11-07
> "The generative music engine needs to be fine tuned to its references if possible.. It needs to sound more like 'aphex twin - ambient works', 'Plaid', 'µ-Ziq', 'Wagon Christ', 'Boards of Canada'."

**Creative reference brief, NOT license to reproduce any existing artist's exact distinctive sound, sampled recording, melody, harmony, named patch, composition, cover art or audio assets.** Compose original AQUORA work inspired by broad genre qualities; no implied artist affiliation. Keep the 21 named meditation intentions and their music-style profiles.

### Translate the reference LIST into independently designed musical attributes
- Early ambient-techno / Selected Ambient Works 85–92 **as broad genre**: hypnotic repetition, strong but restrained pulse, expressive synth bass, spacious pads and sophisticated, evolving melodic overlays; not static nature-only ambience or constantly breaking rhythms.
- Plaid-like broad **melodic electronica**: emotionally engaging short motifs, counterpoint/harmonies and precise, interlocking, asymmetric rhythmic interplay while keeping accessible groove.
- µ-Ziq-like broad **melodic IDM**: playful melodic hooks, complementary synth timbres, articulated rhythmic variations, occasional low-intensity intricate breaks rather than harsh chaotic hyperactivity.
- Wagon Christ-like broad **downtempo/breakbeat**: warm, swung beat articulation, syncopated ghost hits, bouncy melodic-bass phrasing and creative transitions (use only original synthesized sounds, no unlicensed sampling).
- Boards of Canada-like broad **nostalgic analog/lo-fi ambience**: soft detuned/warbling synth timbres, hazy long chord movement, subtly imperfect timing, wistful minor/ambiguous/modal motifs and textured atmosphere. Avoid blatant artist/track signature-copying; support soft spacious variants.
- Combine in AQUORA's **own** musical identity: healing-oriented, water/resonance, evolving generative electronic composition with melodic hooks, musical direction, bass and drum continuity, interlocking voices, nuanced motion and occasional true planned beatless passages. Artistic target, not exact emulation or medical effect.

### Practical FM-1 implementation priorities
1. **Improve composition, not just FX/timbre**: coherent harmonic progression, chord voicing inversions, phrase call/response, motif identity/return, complementary bass melody, organic arrangement structure for 16/32/64, balanced multi-minute growth without generic loop.
2. **Groove**: support kick/snare/hat/hand articulation with dynamic velocities, swing/microtiming, ghost notes, variation/answer fills and natural drum breaks. Drum default need not be aggressive; avoid inexplicable dropout (#soundscape-only-dead-zones).
3. **Synth texture**: within available 16 voices and real-time budget, create a small varied palette of expressive warm FM/analog-like pads, bell/plucks, softened bass, detuned drift, low-cost gentle chorus/modulation, accessible attack/release contours. **No CPU-expensive new FFT, convolution or sample licensing;** make objective headroom check.
4. **Musical modes**: Tune Standard/Cinematic/Neoclassical **and intention profiles** for stronger individuality, without promising literal target-artist presets. A meditative slow intention can be gentle but coherent, not silent. Do not overwrite fixed reference Hz / binaural.
5. Create a **human-listening comparison pack** of representative original 3–8-minute compositions (e.g., melodic ambient techno, intricate gentle IDM, mellow broken-beat, warm nostalgic drift), with corresponding event/role/groove timelines and per-stem renders. Ask owner to judge melody, texture, forward motion, groove, unwanted silences and listenability; no claim audible likeness already reached.
6. Preserve v0.6.7 audio+visual smoothness and input performance; no change to instrument count, save-bank mapping or active transport MIDI deferrals. Focus on targeted measured changes and quality before adding lots of new controls.

Relevant context sources (genre characteristics only): Pitchfork Selected Ambient Works 85–92 https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/223-selected-ambient-works-85-92/ ; Plaid overview https://www.idmdiscovery.com/artist/plaid ; µ-Ziq https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/18307-u-ziq-somerset-avenue-tracks-1992-1995/ ; Wagon Christ https://ra.co/reviews/2228 ; Boards of Canada broad wistful analog-electronica description should be further triangulated in research.

Required post-v0.6.7 work and owner subjective acceptance. Coordinate #34 #43 #44 #9 #40 and soundscape dead zone fix. Do not start a separate build or publish until user explicitly authorizes next release; KIRA-9 untouched.

issue.title: v0.6.7: Enlarge EVOLVE note/hit markers while preserving the graph's design and eight-role readability
issue.body:
## Owner real-device v0.6.7 UI refinement — 2026-11-07

> "The evolve screen is very nice with its graph, but could you make the hits or notes it's showing larger."

**Preserve the current EVOLVE graph's design, role colors, 64-step timeline, live animation, section/phrase text and general layout.** The user likes it; do not redesign. Make individual event marks substantially easier to see on the 240×240 FM-1 LCD, especially when bright backgrounds are enabled.

### Source-verified current behavior
In `device/ui.c` at v0.6.7, EVOLVE second-band display uses 8 role rows `y=t*5u+3u`. For each set bit in `evolve_history[index]`, it currently renders `cv_line(x,y,x+2,y,colors[t])`, a **3px-wide × 1px-high** event marker. `device/app.c` derives that history from per-role event-counter changes, not actual MIDI note pitch/velocity. Don't falsely label these marks as representing specific note heights.

### Desired
- Draw larger, clearly visible event blocks approximately **3–4px wide × 2–3px high** (final tune via real 240×240 renders), keeping marks constrained within each roughly 5px track row.
- Preserve separation between rows and horizontal timing, avoid markers painting over other roles or the playhead. Dense 16th-note passages should remain legible, not become an unbroken solid rectangle. Consider stroke/outline for light and dark theme contrast, not expensive visual effects.
- Show the same events as before with the exact same timing and data. No fake new events, extra per-sample telemetry, or avoidable redraws.
- If the panel is cramped, optimize layout carefully rather than adding scroll or tiny labels; this is a targeted change and owner prefers the existing graph.
- Acceptance: actual 240×240 screenshots/animation for sparse, moderate and dense eight-role cases, both themes and font sizes; assert marker geometry, no clipping/overlap, unchanged performance and input latency (#46).

**Required next corrective release**, not implemented in v0.6.7. Preserve released versions and no competing Work sessions. Related #9/#34/#46/#48 and master tracker #32.

issue.title: v0.6.7: Tone down excessive automatic Lead/Bass glide; retain user MANUAL and expressive musical variation
issue.body:
## Owner physical listening feedback — 2026-11-07

> "It's over doing it with its auto glide a bit.. tone it down."

### Source-grounded behavior
- `device/dsp/engine.c::intention_motion[21][2]` supplies auto Lead/Bass portamento profiles. Example values range roughly **65–220ms** for Lead and **70–210ms** for Bass; many use `glide_mode=1` (Legato).
- `apply_motion_profile` adds **+95ms Lead and +55ms Bass** in Cinematic mode, making some transitions noticeably smeared/over-slid; Neoclassical usually disables glide. In `device/dsp/engine.c` the voice render advances pitch toward target using `glide_ms`, so effect is actually audible.
- User wants **less frequent and less intense automatic glide**, not zero glide across every scene.

### Requirements
1. Rebalance all **21 intentions × 3 styles**, not just one hardcoded intention. Default AUTO glide should be **subtle and musical**; shorten duration and limit how often glide triggers, especially standard melodies and bass anchors; avoid whole melody sounding like continuous portamento. Keep selective expressive legato in appropriate moments and strong glide only as a deliberate manual user choice. Cinematic should no longer blindly add ~95ms/55ms when baseline is already slow.
2. Favor short pitch changes or glide only between genuinely connected/overlapping compatible notes where musically appropriate, with zero or minimal on new detached phrases, large jumps and new section entrances. Avoid unintended out-of-key detours beyond intended note transition, detuned bass kick masking, zipper, stuck notes.
3. **Do not override MANUAL glide/motion settings or SAVE bank intention-specific overrides**; communicate AUTO/MANUAL mode clearly in SOUND. Revert-to-AUTO should use new intention defaults and be immediately audible; preserve motion/glide controls and existing 0.6.6/0.6.7 save migration.
4. Provide level-matched same-seed original 0.6.7 vs proposed AUTO pitch/PCM comparisons for meditative and lively intentions, Standard/Cinematic/Neoclassical and both roles. Quantify slide rates/time and continuity; subjective owner listening checks remain OWNER-UNVERIFIED.
5. Preserve FM-1 DSP headroom, tuning, frequency-lock exact Hz, stereo binaural and audio-first behavior. No new pricey per-sample pitch math or new lag (#46).

**Required next corrective release**, not a published v0.6.7 fix. Related #23, #35, #48, #32; do not start another builder, do not modify KIRA-9, MIDI performance transports deferred.

issue.title: Next AQUORA: Optimized EIN-1-inspired CHORD voicing + TOGETHER/STRUM playback, SOUND controls and musical AUTO profiles
issue.body:
## Owner authorizes importing the EIN-1 STRUM + CHORD *concepts* into original AQUORA, optimized for the FM-1 — 2026-11-07

Owner requests: **"Let's introduce the strum feature/effect from EIN-1 but fully optimized. It can become another setting in the SOUND section (like glide and vibrato), Generative music engine should use it appropriately."** Follow-up: **"we will also introduce the chords too, if the generative music engine is not utilizing chords it should."**

### Historical EIN-1 behavior to preserve intentionally, not wholesale code port
- User previously specified a **CHORD PLAYBACK choice: TOGETHER** (notes sounded simultaneously) **or STRUM** (notes sounded sequentially).
- **STRUM GAP** is a *separate control*, effective **only** while STRUM is selected; reference desired timing range **80–140 ms** when Strum is enabled, with appropriately bounded faster/slower optional refinement if justified.
- **TOGETHER / Strum OFF must introduce NO note-on delay**. Distinguish genuinely simultaneous chord articulation from faux stagger caused by an always-on strum scheduler.
- Intention/music-mode-specific AUTO recommendations for tempo, chord voicing, strum timing, sustain, rhythmic feel and phrase placement. Explicit CUSTOM/MANUAL overrides must be retained, and unlocking restores Auto musical defaults. These were requirements of EIN-1 but are **new to AQUORA** and must be independently engineered and verified, not assumed already implemented.
- Do not copy potentially licensed or inappropriate legacy source verbatim or bring retired EIN-1 code/dependencies into AQUORA. Reuse conceptual behavior through new small optimized engine architecture.

### Existing AQUORA v0.6.7 code facts
- `device/dsp/engine.c::phrase_chord()` already drives harmonic/chord degrees for bass and generated notes. `mode_phrase()` issues Drone/Choir/Harmony notes at the same bar, but there is **no explicit selectable polyphonic chord-voicing + Together/Strum playback model**. Don't claim chords are entirely missing: they exist harmonically, but lack expressive, coherent voicing/voice-leading and a distinct chord/strum articulation system.
- `ornament()` currently has only **four monophonic scheduled-note slots** (Piano/Guitar/Lead/Harmony) for microtiming, not a robust chord scheduler. Build a bounded chord event queue independent of costly per-sample work; don't misuse/corrupt the existing ornaments or physical keys.
- FM-1 uses **16 synth voices**, currently finite voice stealing; all new chord notes require tested voice budgeting, anti-stuck-note and headroom. UI current SOUND Group 6 "Lead / Bass Motion" has four physical knobs used by glide/vibrato; create a discoverable **SOUND > CHORD / STRUM** section (adjacent to Motion) rather than overwriting those four controls.

### Musical behavior required
1. **Real chord-voicing generation**, not merely independent root and harmony coincident notes. Harmonically coherent 2-/3-/occasionally 4-note voicings, inversion selection, register/spacing, controlled note overlap, minimal natural voice-leading and chord resolution; scale/key/intention/mode aware. Intention/style decides harmonic rhythm, density, colorful sus/add/7th-like *original* voicings as suitable, and rests. Keep 16/32/64 statement-answer-development musically distinct; bass/drums stay purposeful and don't disappear during a strum.
2. **Chord mode**: AUTO (intention/style chooses musically appropriate articulation), TOGETHER (true simultaneous) and STRUM (stagger chord tones). Optional OFF/disabled chord layer if needed, with precise distinction from STRUM OFF and per-track mute. If automatic mode uses no strum, scheduling cost ~0.
3. **Strum timing**: adjustable STRUM GAP in milliseconds (historical favored 80–140ms), optional DOWN/UP/ALTERNATE and natural, seeded accent/velocity variation; all note-ons quantized to safe musical intent with limited timing offsets and appropriate gate/sustain. No user-visible control should claim unavailable hardware subdivisions. Never strum every note or every chord automatically.
4. **Role assignment**: Guitar/pluck and strummed keys/chords are the most natural targets; arpeggiated Piano/Harmony/Choir/pads may use alternate voicing or slow spreads. Bass and Lead should not indiscriminately strum, and kick/drums must stay punchy. Rhythm/style can choose ambient loose/downward, shimmering slow arpeggio, playful melodic IDM syncopation or clean Together accents, preserving AQUORA's calming identity. Match existing 21 intentions × 3 music modes and upcoming optional experimental rhythms (#51).
5. **SOUND UI**: Clear, readable 240×240 `CHORDS: AUTO / TOGETHER / STRUM`, `STRUM GAP: N ms` active only for STRUM, plus accessible `VOICE/INVERSION` and optionally `DIRECTION` or `SUSTAIN` with four-knob navigation. Show Auto vs Manual, effective values and selected harmonic role; avoid duplicating global chord settings unnecessarily. Ensure robust SELECT/EDIT navigation and live control responsiveness (#35/#46), no dead controls. Manual controls may provide a playable chord-trigger mode for physical keys if safe, but must not replace existing Play Along/perfect-key behavior or create unwanted multi-note triggers.
6. **Evolve integration**: coherent chord progression/strumming roles change purposefully across planned song sections, returning motifs, harmony, and 16/32/64; Strum and Chord notes count as true role events in mixers and EVOLVE graph (#49). Avoid extended Nature-only gaps (#47) and limit chord voicings under already-high role polyphony.
7. **Persistence**: Save/restore chord and strum mode + manual settings in each of the four arrangement banks and appropriate startup defaults; versioned migration preserving all pre-v0.6.7/v0.6.7 banks (CRC, IDs, no silent bank destruction). Automatic intention/style changes should recompute unlocked STRUM/CHORD profile only, not override manual edits/locks. Physical master at 0 must not affect internal timing.

### HARD optimization & performance requirement (not optional)
- **Fix PLAY-only knob/button lag (#46) before evaluating/expanding playback-time chord work.** No blocking input-scan/graphics/flash writes caused by chord additions; prompt control dispatch at full polyphony.
- Precompute chord notes/offsets at phrase/step control rate or ahead of time; bounded fixed-size event ring, zero dynamic allocation, constant-time or tiny per-frame event dispatch; **no expensive polyphonic planning or strum calculations in per-sample DSP callback**.
- Reserve voices (e.g. cap simultaneous strummed notes if near 16-voice ceiling), predictable overflow handling, no voice starvation of Bass and other anchors, hard STOP/scene/mode/key-change/panic clears pending strums and note tails, stable manual play and external MIDI non-interference. Do not increase XRUN/callback budgets, clipping, missing meters or control delay.
- Verify release/native + forced-single-core/WASM, eight updater paths as applicable, post-gain stems, note timings (TOGETHER simultaneity / STRUM 80–140ms gap with tolerances), correct key/scale/voicing, CPU p95/p99 and voice count, drum/bass continuity, SAVE/LOAD/migrations and long soak at 21 scenes × 3 modes × 3 lengths, across high voice load/Frequency Lock/binaural/Nature. Human sound quality & hardware playability **OWNER-UNVERIFIED** until actual FM-1 review.

**Release classification:** NEW NEXT-BUILD P0/P1 feature, **NOT part of published v0.6.7**. No active build launched by writing this issue. Preserve v0.6.7 and v0.6.6 references, both MIDI performance transports owner-deferred, AIR required, KIRA-9 untouched.

Related #23 (motion profiles), #34/#43 macro evolution, #46 PLAY-only input lag, #47 Nature-only gaps, #48 original ambient IDM inspiration, #49 graph, #50 tame glide, #51 optional IDM drums, #32 active issue/owner-comment requirement tracker.

issue.title: AQUORA: Subtle experimental IDM rolls, build-ups, musical breaks and breakout/return transitions
issue.body:
## Owner's v0.6.7 physical listening / creative direction — 2026-11-07

> "we should have the rolls, build ups and break outs as we examined in other firmware but a toned down more experimental version that fits with the artists i referenced to you."

**Add deliberate, subtle and adventurous ROLLS, BUILDS, BREAKS/BREAKDOWNS, and BREAKOUT/RETURN moments** to AQUORA's own intention-aware, evolving *original* melodic ambient IDM / downtempo compositions. Relevant broad references already documented in #48: early ambient electronic music, intricate but musical melodic IDM, relaxed broken beats, warm nostalgic textures and restrained left-field rhythmic detail. **Do not copy distinctive tracks, artist signature phrases, samples or source code.** Avoid predictable giant EDM risers/drops, rave snare crescendo clichés, frantic maximalism, hard brick-wall crashes or nature-only voids.

### Grounding: what is missing from v0.6.7
- The prior [SIREN concept review](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/main/validation/SIREN_GENERATIVE_ENGINE_REVIEW_2026-11-06.md) identified intro/groove/break/build/return **macro-form** and rhythmic event planning on different timescales as useful. It explicitly proposed an original, calmer AQUORA implementation; no licensed SIREN source should be copied.
- In released `device/dsp/engine.c`, `song_section()` plans five simple section identities, but `drum_trigger()` largely triggers 16-step kick/hand/shaker patterns and a few probabilistic offbeats. This is *not* a complete arrangement-aware roll → build → contrast → breakout/reentry vocabulary. `role_target` currently switches both bass and drums off in section 3, and sometimes produces owner-reported unexplained soundscape-only gaps (#47). Guard against repeating that failure.
- New optional experimental drum-character modes and kick clarity are in #51; intentional composition/evolution is in #34; chords/strum in #52. Implement **one coherent arranger**, not multiple disconnected randomized effect routines or duplicated control pages.

### Sound design and composition behavior
1. **Subtle rolls / micro-fills:** tasteful hand/snare, hats, rim/textural brush, low-kick ghost and occasional tiny flams/ratchets with intentional placement (phrase endings, answers, transitions). Use controlled quiet-to-loud velocity, occasional asymmetry, syncopation, odd subdivisions and natural spacing, not blanket machine-gun 16th/32nd rolls. Maintain clear, satisfying low kick and full drum separation (all 19 kits, #18).
2. **Gradual builds:** over 1–4 bars (longer where 64-step structure supports), evolve complementary elements—hi-hat density, syncopation, filtered sound color, chord inversion/strum tension, bass punctuation, pads/textures and occasional melodic counterpoint. Smoothly increase movement and interest, **not necessarily overall loudness or CPU/voice count**; use restrained rhythmic escalation and coherent harmonic anticipation.
3. **Breaks / breakdowns / hush:** musically earned reductions—brief muted kick with a meaningful melodic, bass, chord or rhythmic through-line; sometimes a deliberate beatless ambient interlude. Do **not** create arbitrary prolonged Nature-only dead zones. Break length, which anchors remain, and re-entry must follow intention, mode, variation, song section and phrase position; give extremely quiet intentions tasteful minimum action without forced full drums.
4. **Breakouts / returns / resolutions:** a recognizable groove/motif re-enters after a break with satisfying clear bass kick, varied drum accents, resumed harmony/strummed-chord texture, occasional small melody variation. Avoid harsh EDM drop and excessive amplitude spikes. Use motif memory and meaningful A/A′/B/resolution across 16/32/64.
5. **Progressive probability:** intent/style/energy and user choice control how often these occur. Standard stays tasteful, Cinematic broad and spacious, Neoclassical delicate and infrequent, and **Experimental IDM / Ambient Broken** option (#51) is more exploratory yet musical. Give user straightforward control of **TRANSITION ACTIVITY** or **FILL CHARACTER** (Auto / Gentle / Experimental / Off) only if clear and nonduplicative with drum style; avoid sprawling UI. AUTO chooses musically appropriate density; if user turns fills OFF, keep basic groove and appropriate macro arrangements. Respect manual drum OFF, mute, solo, locks, Freeze, bank save/restore, live controls.
6. **True multiscale structure:** a fill at a 16-step bar boundary is not the same as a 32/64-step phrase buildup and not the same as a multi-phrase section bridge. Keep corresponding arrangement logic separate but coherent. Underlying pulse and note event scheduling must remain deterministic and repeatable with seed, appropriate swing/velocity envelopes and selective ratchets.

### Optimization and regression priority
- **#46 P0 PLAY-only knob/button latency MUST be fixed/verified before introducing new playback load.** Keep music scheduling out of per-sample DSP; use precomputed bounded fixed-size phrase/step event plans or cheap event flags, fixed queue with explicit overload policy, no dynamic allocation/FFTs/new audio callback work.
- FM-1 44.1kHz real-time audio, 16-voice headroom, stable 20 FPS visuals, smooth single-core fallback, limited flash/power. Overlapping fast drum transients, strummed chords and FX must not clip or steal all lead/bass voices. No stuck sustained envelopes after STOP/scene/tempo changes.
- Avoid unlicensed samples; original synth transients and patterns only.

### Acceptance
- Same-seed rendered **full mix + isolated drum/bass/chord stems** with labeled section/event timelines, comparing baseline v0.6.7 and proposed. Demonstrate actual distinct roll/build/break/return episodes with timing and dynamic meaning and clear restrained low-end.
- All 21 intentions × three music modes × 16/32/64 lengths across representative seeded variation levels and an extended multi-hour simulated arrangement. Check rarity/context, not a fixed forced roll every bar. Include Standard vs experimental drum character toggles, Freeze, STOP/PLAY, 4 Save Banks/migration, New Song/Reroll, user mutes, Nature-only prevention and return-home motif.
- Capture audio callback p95/p99, XRUN, audio headroom, actual control event-to-visible update latency with music PLAY vs STOP, visual frame p95/p99, bass/kick tonal integrity, max events/CPU and single-core fallback. Human listening and FM-1 subjective acceptance remains **OWNER-UNVERIFIED** until owner tests.
- Do not call the feature complete from event counters alone; examine actual sounds and musically meaningful listening clips.

**Disposition:** NEW next-release requirement, not present/accepted in published v0.6.7. Track in main #32 requirement matrix and active queue at next exclusive owner-authorized Work build. Preserve v0.6.6/v0.6.7 and GitHub backups; both USB/BLE performance MIDI deferred, AIR required, KIRA-9 untouched. Related #18, #34, #43, #46–#48, #51–#52.

## OWNER PHYSICAL v0.6.7 TEST + RECOVERED ORIGINAL AIR DESIGN — 2026-11-07

Owner reports: "**The AIR mode seems to be working however the effects for it make it nearly impossible to detect that it's working or not... I thought we would have implemented the features we talked about where you can change and evolve the music just by waving your hand, etc.**"

**This is a major previously approved AIR scope gap, not just a request to make the reverb louder.** The owner wants a **touchless Kaoss-Pad-inspired musical performance control**, with BLE-antenna hand proximity controlling BOTH audible effects and the evolving generative arrangement. The original discussions specified track/drum/whole mix targeting, calibrated 0–100% normalized AIR, sensitivity/smoothing/depth/invert, large live meters, Momentary/Hold-Latch/**gesture-triggered** modes, effects including echo/ambience/filter/modulation and **musical events including harmonies, arpeggiation, swells, fills and evolving activity**. AIR OFF by default, optimized low-rate RF path. Original JIANT/JIANT 10.35 passive proximity model was a reference, not permission to copy source or claim true 2D motion tracking.

### Verified CURRENT v0.6.7 behavior
- `device/air_sensor.h`: FAR/NEAR RSSI calibration with packet freshness (800ms), filtered RSSI smoothing (.36), normalized proximity, RADIO OFF/STARTING/LISTENING/ACTIVE and lost-signal statuses. **This is passive one-dimensional radio signal attenuation, not an actual hand/gesture camera or precise distance tracker; it needs meaningful external radio advertisements/signal.**
- `device/app.c::app_frame`: every ~40ms, `plat_air_sample` → `aq_air_update` → control #70 only, setting normalized `engine.air_target`. Existing AIR knobs are RADIO, FOCUS, CALIBRATE, HOLD on SENSOR tab and FX (0..2), DEPTH, MANUAL AIR on mapping tab.
- `device/dsp/engine.c::apply_fx`: AIR target smoothly boosts **reverb wet to .8**, **delay wet to .7**, or both. `sr_render` increases send level (all tracks or selected). **There is NO RSSI-proximity-to-song-evolution, phrase-trigger, role change, drum fill, harmonic/chord modulation or arpeggio generator.** The current implementation therefore cannot meet the original musical gesturing request despite basic hand data and FX control.
- `device/ui.c` already displays RAW/SMOOTH/PKT/s, AIR % and wet %. Yet user hears too little effect. **Presence of input meters is not evidence of perceivable applied audio.** Test and tune actual audible selected-target routing, base send, wet dry, masking and FX mix vs correct input.

### Release requirements

**P0 A: Make AIR EFFECTS observably audible and visibly traceable**
1. Hand far → near → far, holding near, short wave and release: show trustworthy signal/packet/confidence/normalized proximity and **actual FX/parameter change** with value/name/target.
